question: Select the option that has used the correct tense.
option_1: Yesterday, we will be painting the door when a neighbour stops by to say hello.
option_2: Yesterday, we are painting the door when a neighbour stop by to say hello.
option_3: Yesterday, we was painting the door when a neighbour stopping by to say hello.
option_4: Yesterday, we were painting the door when a neighbour stopped by to say hello.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Yesterday, we were painting the door when a neighbour stopped by to say hello.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The adverb "Yesterday" fixes the action firmly in the past, so the whole sentence must be in the past tense.

• A longer background action interrupted by a shorter one uses past continuous (was/were + -ing) for the longer action and simple past (V2) for the interrupting action: "we were painting the door when a neighbour stopped by".

◦ Correct: Yesterday, we were painting the door when a neighbour stopped by to say hello.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 wrongly uses the future "will be painting" with "Yesterday".

• Option 2 uses the present "are painting / stop"; Option 3 uses the wrong plural form "we was" and the non-finite "stopping".

NOTE

• Structure: When + past simple interrupts an ongoing past continuous action — "While I was reading, the phone rang."

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

The coaches decided to _____ the regulations more strictly because the candidates were not paying attention during their training sessions.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. enforce.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Enforce" means to make sure that a rule or law is obeyed; to impose compliance. Rules/regulations are things one "enforces". (लागू करना / पालन कराना)

◦ Correct: The coaches decided to enforce the regulations more strictly ...

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "enjoy", Option 2 "provide" and Option 4 "supply" do not collocate with "regulations more strictly" and change the intended meaning.

NOTE

• Common collocations: enforce a law / rule / regulation / discipline / ban. Related word: "reinforce" (to strengthen).

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

I checked the ____________ to see if it will rain or not.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. weather.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Weather" (a noun) means the state of the atmosphere — rain, sunshine, temperature, etc. One checks the "weather" to know if it will rain. (मौसम)

◦ Correct: I checked the weather to see if it will rain or not.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• These are homophones: "whether" (a conjunction showing a choice — whether or not), "wither" (a verb — to dry up / shrivel) and "wether" (a castrated ram) do not fit.

NOTE

• Remember the trio: weather (मौसम) vs whether (क्या / चाहे) vs wither (मुरझाना). The blank needs the atmospheric noun "weather".

question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the underlined word in the given sentence.

Although she is virtuous in her deeds, people misinterpret her because of her open and bold nature.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. wicked.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Virtuous" means having high moral standards; righteous and good. Its antonym is "wicked", meaning morally bad or evil. (सदाचारी का विलोम — दुष्ट)

◦ Example: A virtuous person does good; a wicked person does harm.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 3 "moral" and Option 4 "commendable" are synonyms of virtuous.

• Option 1 "sane" (of sound mind) is unrelated.

NOTE

• Synonyms of virtuous: moral, righteous, upright, honourable. Antonyms: wicked, sinful, immoral, corrupt.

question: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Concieve.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Concieve" is misspelt. The correct spelling is "conceive", meaning to form an idea / to become pregnant. (कल्पना करना / गर्भधारण करना)

◦ Correct spelling: CON + CEIVE.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• "Separate", "Accessible" and "Convenience" are all correctly spelt.

NOTE

• Spelling rule: "i before e, except after c" — so it is receive, deceive, conceive, perceive (after 'c' → 'ei').

question:
Select the most appropriate option that can replace the underlined segment in the given sentence.

No sooner had they left their home that it started raining heavily.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. their home than it started.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The structure "No sooner ... than" is a fixed pair (not "no sooner ... that"). It follows inversion: "No sooner had + subject + V3 than + past simple".

◦ Correct: No sooner had they left their home than it started raining heavily.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 wrongly keeps "that" and uses "start"; Option 2 wrongly uses the present "starts"; Option 3 uses the wrong spelling "there" (should be the possessive "their").

NOTE

• Similar correlatives with inversion: "Hardly/Scarcely ... when", "No sooner ... than". Both describe one event happening immediately after another.

question:
Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given phrase.

Something that has the quality of being easily broken
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Brittle.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Brittle" means hard but liable to break easily; fragile. It exactly fits "something that has the quality of being easily broken". (भंगुर / आसानी से टूटने वाला)

◦ Example: Glass and dry twigs are brittle.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "Broken" describes something already broken, not the quality of breaking easily.

• Option 3 "Damage" is a noun/verb for harm; Option 4 "Hard" is the near opposite here.

NOTE

• Related words: fragile (easily damaged), frail (weak), flimsy (thin and weak). Antonyms of brittle: sturdy, tough, durable.

question:
Select the correct idiom to substitute the underlined segment in the following sentence.

Sean is notorious for revealing the secrets about the company.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Spilling the beans.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "to spill the beans" means to reveal secret information (usually accidentally or carelessly). It matches "revealing the secrets about the company". (राज़ खोल देना)

◦ Example: He spilled the beans about the surprise party.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "in bad blood" (feeling of hatred), Option 2 "bite the bullet" (to face a difficult situation bravely) and Option 4 "bite the dust" (to fail / die) do not fit.

NOTE

• Similar idioms about revealing secrets: "let the cat out of the bag", "give the game away", "blow the whistle"

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

I have a __________ for reading and want to become a writer when I grow up.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. passion.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Passion" means a strong, intense enthusiasm or love for something. "A passion for reading" is a natural collocation showing deep interest. (गहरी रुचि / जुनून)

◦ Correct: I have a passion for reading and want to become a writer ...

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "tallow" (animal fat used for candles/soap) is unrelated.

• Option 2 "unity" (oneness) and Option 3 "dream" do not collocate with "a ___ for reading" as naturally ("passion for" is the fixed pattern).

NOTE

• Collocation: "a passion for" (music/reading/art). Related words: zeal, fervour, enthusiasm, ardour.

question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined words in the given sentence.

Solving the riddle given by our teacher is farther beyond our capacity.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. far.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Far beyond" is the correct phrase meaning well outside / much more than one's capacity. "Farther" refers to physical/literal distance, which does not suit an abstract "capacity".

◦ Correct: Solving the riddle ... is far beyond our capacity.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "fair" (just / light-coloured) and Option 2 "fare" (a bus/train charge or food) are homophones that do not fit.

• Option 3 "farthest" is a superlative of distance and is wrong here.

NOTE

• "Farther/farthest" → physical distance; "further/furthest" → extent/degree. With "beyond our capacity" (figurative), we simply use "far beyond"

question:
Select the most appropriate idiom that can substitute the underlined words in the given sentence.

I heard management is planning to transfer me to another department and demote me. I need to confirm if this is true by hearing it directly from the person involved and from my manager.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. straight from the horse's mouth.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "straight from the horse's mouth" means from the original, most reliable/authoritative source. It matches "hearing it directly from the person involved". (विश्वसनीय स्रोत से सीधे)

◦ Example: I got the news straight from the horse's mouth — the CEO himself.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "on pins and needles" (anxious / nervous), Option 3 "in the seventh heaven" (extremely happy) and Option 4 "bearing a grudge" (holding resentment) do not fit.

NOTE

• Related idioms of reliable information: "from a reliable source", "first-hand information"

question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

There has been / an increase of the number / of road / accidents recently.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. an increase of the number.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The correct preposition is "in", not "of", after "increase" when referring to a rise in quantity: "an increase in the number".

◦ Correct: There has been an increase in the number of road accidents recently.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• "There has been", "of road" and "accidents recently" are all correct.

NOTE

• Use "an increase in" (a rise in amount/level) — increase in prices, increase in temperature. "Increase of" is used mainly with a figure (an increase of 10%).

question:
Select the option that rectifies the error in the usage of the future tense in the given sentence.

Shivani go to school tomorrow for prize distribution.
option_1: Shivani will go to school tomorrow for prize distribution.
option_2: Shivani has gone to school tomorrow for prize distribution.
option_3: Shivani had gone to school tomorrow for prize distribution.
option_4: Shivani goes to school tomorrow for prize distribution.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Shivani will go to school tomorrow for prize distribution.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The adverb "tomorrow" indicates the future, which requires "will + base verb": "Shivani will go".

◦ Correct: Shivani will go to school tomorrow for prize distribution.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "has gone" (present perfect) and Option 3 "had gone" (past perfect) are past forms and clash with "tomorrow".

• Option 4 "goes" (simple present) does not express the future intention correctly here.

NOTE

• Simple Future: subject + will/shall + V1 (I will go, She will come). Time markers: tomorrow, next week, soon, later.

question:
Rectify the sentence by selecting the correct spelling of the underlined word from the options.

He was startled by the loud thander during the storm.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. thunder.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The correctly spelt word is "thunder" — the loud rumbling sound that follows a flash of lightning. (गर्जन / बादल की गरज)

◦ Correct: He was startled by the loud thunder during the storm.

• Spelling key: THUN + DER.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• "thondar", "thundar" and "thundre" are all misspellings of "thunder".

NOTE

• Related words: thunderstorm, thunderous (very loud), thunderbolt (a flash of lightning with thunder), lightning (the flash).

question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.

Osmium is heavy metal in the periodic table.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. the heaviest.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Comparing one item with all others ("in the periodic table") requires the superlative degree. The superlative of "heavy" is "the heaviest".

◦ Correct: Osmium is the heaviest metal in the periodic table.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "more heavy" and Option 4 "the most heavy" are wrong because short adjectives like "heavy" form degrees with "-ier/-iest", not "more/most".

• Option 2 "heavier" (comparative) needs "than" and compares only two things.

NOTE

• Degrees of "heavy": heavy – heavier (than) – the heaviest. Osmium is indeed the densest/heaviest naturally occurring element.

question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word.

Excessive
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Moderate.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Excessive" means too much; more than necessary. Its antonym is "moderate", meaning reasonable, limited and not extreme. (अत्यधिक का विलोम — संयमित)

◦ Example: An excessive amount vs a moderate amount.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 3 "Inordinate" (unusually large / excessive) is a synonym of excessive.

• Option 2 "Flow" and Option 4 "Desirable" are unrelated.

NOTE

• Synonyms of excessive: exorbitant, inordinate, immoderate, undue. Antonyms: moderate, reasonable, limited, scanty.

question:
Select the option that correctly rectifies the underlined spelling error.

The scientist made an appauling discovery about the environmental impact of the drug.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. appalling.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The correct spelling is "appalling", meaning shocking, horrifying or extremely bad. (भयावह / अत्यंत बुरा)

◦ Correct: The scientist made an appalling discovery about the environmental impact of the drug.

• Spelling key: AP + PALL + ING (double 'p', double 'l').

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• "apalling", "appaulling" and "appawling" are all misspellings.

NOTE

• Related word: "appal/appall" (to horrify). Synonyms of appalling: dreadful, horrific, atrocious, ghastly.

question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

He was constantly / gazing on the / crime scene to / find some clues.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. gazing on the.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The verb "gaze" takes the preposition "at" (or "upon"), not "on". So it should be "gazing at the crime scene".

◦ Correct: He was constantly gazing at the crime scene to find some clues.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• "He was constantly", "crime scene to" and "find some clues" are all correct.

NOTE

• Verb + preposition: gaze at, stare at, look at, glance at. We "gaze at" something we look at long and steadily.

question:
Select the most appropriate word from the options to fill in the blank.

Adithya ordered a juicy _________________ cooked to perfection at the highway restaurant.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. steak.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Steak" is a thick slice of meat (especially beef) for grilling or frying. "A juicy steak cooked to perfection" fits a restaurant context. (मांस का टुकड़ा — स्टेक)

◦ Correct: Adithya ordered a juicy steak cooked to perfection ...

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• "stake" (a wooden post / a bet / a share) and "steak" are homophones; "stink" (a bad smell) and "stoke" (to add fuel to a fire) do not fit.

NOTE

• Homophones: steak (मांस) vs stake (दांव / हिस्सेदारी). "At stake" means at risk.

question:
Select the word that is OPPOSITE in meaning to the underlined word in the given sentence.

The name should also be beneficial to a strong, long-lasting marketing campaign.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Detrimental.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Beneficial" means helpful, favourable or advantageous. Its antonym is "detrimental", meaning harmful or damaging. (लाभदायक का विलोम — हानिकारक)

◦ Example: Exercise is beneficial; smoking is detrimental.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Desirable" and Option 3 "Advantageous" are synonyms of beneficial.

• Option 4 "Causal" (relating to a cause) is unrelated.

NOTE

• Synonyms of beneficial: advantageous, favourable, helpful, valuable. Antonyms: detrimental, harmful, damaging, adverse.

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

It was just before noon on June 26, 1975, and my friend and I were out exploring the bustling by-lanes of Delhi's Karol Bagh, unaware that the Emergency had been declared, and that it would change our lives in ways we could have never ___1___. Though Indira Gandhi had herself announced the Emergency in a national broadcast at 8 am, IST, the news took its own time to reach the common people who went about their business as always. However, two hours into our outing, we ___2___ something was wrong. The pavement shops began to thin out as we watched and the bigger outlets too looked ready to ___3___; many of them worked behind half-downed shutters. We were young but fancied ourselves as political animals, which at the time was shorthand for being passionately anti-Congress and anti-Indira. There was no way we were going to head home without knowing what had happened. There was already considerable excitement in our small friends' circle over two ___4___ developments: the June 12, 1975 Allahabad high court ruling unseating Indira for electoral malpractices and the Congress's unexpected defeat in the State election in Gujarat. The Supreme Court had allowed Indira to continue as prime minister but that did not ___5___ our joy; it was a technical reprieve that did not lessen the political blow she had received.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. imagined.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Imagined" means thought of / pictured in the mind. The Emergency would change their lives "in ways we could have never imagined" — i.e., never anticipated or thought possible. (कल्पना की)

◦ Correct: ... it would change our lives in ways we could have never imagined.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "undermined" (weakened), Option 2 "betrothed" (engaged to marry) and Option 3 "targeted" (aimed at) do not fit the sense of "could have never ___".

NOTE

• Collocation: "in ways we could never have imagined" is a common expression conveying something completely unexpected.

Additional Information

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. wrap up.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The phrasal verb "wrap up" means to finish / close down (business for the day). The bigger outlets "looked ready to wrap up", working behind half-downed shutters — i.e., about to shut. (बंद करना / समेटना)

◦ Correct: ... the bigger outlets too looked ready to wrap up; many of them worked behind half-downed shutters.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "open up" is the opposite; Option 2 "pop up" (appear suddenly) and Option 3 "chicken out" (back out from fear) do not fit shops closing.

NOTE

• "Wrap up" also means to summarise/conclude ("let's wrap up the meeting") or to dress warmly ("wrap up well").

Additional Information

• Options 3 "flaws" and 4 "mistakes" carry a negative sense that contradicts the "excitement" the events caused.

NOTE

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 5.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. dampen.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Dampen" means to reduce / lessen (a feeling such as enthusiasm or joy). The Supreme Court's technical reprieve "did not dampen our joy" — i.e., did not lessen it. (कम करना / फीका करना)

◦ Correct: ... but that did not dampen our joy; it was a technical reprieve ...

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "adopted" is grammatically and contextually wrong.

• Option 3 "magnified" (increased) is the opposite; Option 4 "diminished" is close in meaning but the fixed collocation here is "dampen (someone's) joy/spirits/enthusiasm".

NOTE

• Common collocation: "dampen one's spirits / enthusiasm / mood". Synonyms: dishearten, deflate, discourage.

question: In September 2023, which Chief Minister of an Indian state won the Lee Kuan Yew Exchange Fellowship for his distinguished contribution to public service?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Himanta Biswa Sarma.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In September 2023, Himanta Biswa Sarma, the Chief Minister of Assam, was conferred the prestigious Lee Kuan Yew Exchange Fellowship for his distinguished contribution to public service. (हिमंता बिस्वा सरमा — असम)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The Lee Kuan Yew Exchange Fellowship was instituted by the government of Singapore in honour of its founding Prime Minister Lee Kuan Yew to promote exchange between eminent personalities.

• Himanta Biswa Sarma became the Chief Minister of Assam in May 2021.

NOTE

• Assam's capital is Dispur; its Governor and Chief Minister head the executive. Assam is famous for tea, silk (Muga) and the one-horned rhinoceros of Kaziranga.

question: Gulbarga and Bidar style of architecture was patronised by which of the following dynasties?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Bahmani dynasty.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Gulbarga and Bidar styles of architecture were patronised by the Bahmani dynasty (Bahmani Sultanate) of the Deccan. Gulbarga and later Bidar served as their capitals. (बहमनी वंश)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• The Bahmani Sultanate was founded in 1347 by Alauddin Bahman Shah (Hasan Gangu), with its first capital at Gulbarga, later shifted to Bidar.

• Notable structures include the Jama Masjid at Gulbarga and the Madrasa of Mahmud Gawan at Bidar.

NOTE

• After the Bahmani Sultanate's decline, it broke into the five Deccan Sultanates — Bijapur, Golconda, Ahmadnagar, Bidar and Berar.

question: Which food is a good source of complete protein?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Eggs.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Eggs" are a good source of complete protein — a protein that contains all nine essential amino acids the body cannot make on its own. (अंडे — संपूर्ण प्रोटीन)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Complete proteins are mostly of animal origin (eggs, milk, meat, fish); plant sources like spinach, lentils and rice are usually "incomplete" (lacking one or more essential amino acids).

• Combining pulses with cereals (dal + rice) can together provide complete protein.

NOTE

• Proteins are made of amino acids; there are 20 amino acids, of which 9 are essential (must come from food). Protein is called the "body-building" nutrient.

question: The property of rock or soil that indicates the ability of allowing fluids to flow through it is called:
solution_text:
The correct answer is Permeability.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Permeability" is the property of a rock or soil that indicates its ability to allow fluids (water, oil, gas) to flow through it via its interconnected pores. (पारगम्यता)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• A related term is porosity — the amount of empty (pore) space in a rock; a rock can be porous yet not very permeable if the pores are not connected.

• Sandstone is highly permeable, whereas clay has low permeability.

NOTE

• Permeable rocks form aquifers (which store and transmit groundwater). Impermeable layers below them are called aquicludes/aquitards.

question: Who among the following was NOT associated with the 'Prarthana Sabha'?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Mahatma Gandhi.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Mahatma Gandhi was NOT associated with the Prarthana Sabha (Prarthana Samaj). It was founded in 1867 in Bombay by Atmaram Pandurang, with R. G. Bhandarkar and Mahadev Govind Ranade as its prominent members. (प्रार्थना सभा — महात्मा गांधी संबंधित नहीं थे)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The Prarthana Samaj was a socio-religious reform movement in western India (Maharashtra), inspired by the Brahmo Samaj, that worked against caste rigidity, child marriage and for widow remarriage and women's education.

• Keshab Chandra Sen influenced its founding.

NOTE

• Reform bodies: Brahmo Samaj (Raja Ram Mohan Roy, 1828), Arya Samaj (Dayananda Saraswati, 1875), Prarthana Samaj (Atmaram Pandurang, 1867).

question: Air and National Defence are examples of which of the following goods?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Public goods.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Air and National Defence are examples of "public goods" — goods that are non-excludable (no one can be prevented from using them) and non-rivalrous (one person's use does not reduce availability to others). (सार्वजनिक वस्तुएँ)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Public goods are generally provided by the government because private markets under-provide them (the "free-rider" problem).

• Other examples: street lighting, public parks, lighthouses, roads.

NOTE

• Classification by rivalry/excludability: Private goods (both), Public goods (neither), Common goods (rivalrous, non-excludable — e.g., fish stocks), Club goods (non-rivalrous, excludable — e.g., cable TV).

question: Captain Hawkins visited India during the reign of:
solution_text:
The correct answer is Jahangir.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Captain William Hawkins visited India (the Mughal court at Agra) in 1608–1611 during the reign of the Mughal emperor Jahangir. He came as an emissary of the English East India Company / King James I. (जहाँगीर)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Later, Sir Thomas Roe came to Jahangir's court (1615–1619) as the ambassador of King James I and secured trading rights for the English.

• Jahangir (r. 1605–1627) was the son of Akbar and was married to Nur Jahan.

NOTE

• Mughal succession: Babur → Humayun → Akbar → Jahangir → Shah Jahan → Aurangzeb.

question: Which type of molecules show dipole-dipole interaction?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Molecules possessing permanent dipole.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Dipole-dipole interactions occur between molecules possessing a permanent dipole, i.e., polar molecules where there is a permanent separation of positive and negative charge. (स्थायी द्विध्रुव वाले अणु)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• A permanent dipole arises when atoms of different electronegativity are bonded (e.g., HCl), creating partial charges (δ+ and δ–).

• Molecules with only transient/temporary dipoles show weaker London dispersion forces.

NOTE

• Types of van der Waals forces: dipole-dipole, dipole-induced dipole and London dispersion forces. The strongest such attraction is the hydrogen bond (a special dipole-dipole interaction).

question: Mahatma Gandhi Kashi Vidyapith was founded by Shiv Prasad Gupta and Bhagwan Das in the year _______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1921.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Mahatma Gandhi Kashi Vidyapith (at Varanasi) was founded in 1921 by Shiv Prasad Gupta and Bhagwan Das. It was inaugurated by Mahatma Gandhi as a national university during the Non-Cooperation Movement. (काशी विद्यापीठ — 1921)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• During the Non-Cooperation Movement (1920–22), several national institutions were set up as alternatives to British-run bodies — Kashi Vidyapith, Jamia Millia Islamia, Gujarat Vidyapith and Bihar Vidyapith.

• It was renamed "Mahatma Gandhi Kashi Vidyapith" in Gandhi's honour.

NOTE

• Jamia Millia Islamia was founded in 1920 at Aligarh (later shifted to Delhi); Gujarat Vidyapith was founded by Gandhi in 1920.

question: From which of the following countries was the concept of the Fundamental Duties borrowed?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Russia.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The concept of Fundamental Duties in the Indian Constitution was borrowed from the Constitution of the erstwhile USSR (Russia). (मौलिक कर्तव्य — रूस/सोवियत संघ से)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Fundamental Duties were added by the 42nd Amendment Act, 1976, on the recommendation of the Swaran Singh Committee, and are listed in Article 51A (Part IVA).

• Originally 10 duties; the 86th Amendment (2002) added the 11th duty (education of children aged 6–14).

NOTE

• Borrowed features: DPSP → Ireland; Fundamental Rights → USA; Parliamentary system → Britain; Emergency provisions → Germany (Weimar); Fundamental Duties → USSR (Russia).

question: Darshana Jhaveri, a famous Manipuri dancer, was awarded the Padma Shri in which of the following years?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 2002.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Darshana Jhaveri, a renowned exponent of the Manipuri classical dance, was honoured with the Padma Shri in the year 2002. (दर्शना झावेरी — मणिपुरी नृत्य — पद्म श्री 2002)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• She is one of the famous Jhaveri sisters (Nayana, Ranjana, Suverna and Darshana), who greatly popularised Manipuri dance.

• Manipuri is the classical dance form of Manipur, often based on themes of Radha–Krishna (Raslila).

NOTE

• The eight classical dance forms of India: Bharatanatyam, Kathak, Kathakali, Kuchipudi, Odissi, Manipuri, Mohiniyattam and Sattriya.

question: For how many days is the Chhat Puja celebrated?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Four.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Chhath Puja is celebrated over four days. It is a festival dedicated to the Sun God (Surya) and Chhathi Maiya, mainly observed in Bihar, Jharkhand, eastern Uttar Pradesh and Nepal. (छठ पूजा — चार दिन)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The four days are: Nahay Khay, Kharna (Lohanda), Sandhya Arghya (evening offering to the setting sun) and Usha Arghya (morning offering to the rising sun).

• Devotees offer arghya to the sun while standing in water and observe a strict fast.

NOTE

• Chhath is celebrated in the month of Kartika (October–November), about six days after Diwali.

question: The Maukharies ruled over ________ in western Uttar Pradesh, which later on replaced Pataliputra as the political centre of northern India.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kanauj.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Maukharis ruled over Kanauj (Kannauj) in western Uttar Pradesh, which later replaced Pataliputra as the chief political centre of northern India. (मौखरी वंश — कन्नौज)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Kanauj rose to prominence and later became the capital of Harshavardhana and the object of the famous Tripartite Struggle among the Palas, Pratiharas and Rashtrakutas.

• The Maukharis had their base around Kanauj after the decline of the Guptas.

NOTE

• The Tripartite Struggle (8th–9th century) for control of Kanauj was ultimately won by the Gurjara-Pratiharas.

question: Kishori Amonkar, one of the finest classical singers of Hindustani music, was from which state?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Maharashtra.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Kishori Amonkar, one of the finest exponents of Hindustani classical (vocal) music, was from Maharashtra (born in Mumbai in 1932). (किशोरी अमोनकर — महाराष्ट्र)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• She belonged to the Jaipur-Atrauli gharana and was the daughter of the noted singer Mogubai Kurdikar.

• She was honoured with the Padma Bhushan (1987) and the Padma Vibhushan (2002).

NOTE

• A gharana is a school/style of Hindustani music. Famous gharanas include Gwalior, Agra, Kirana, Jaipur-Atrauli and Patiala.

question: 'Gaur Maria' dance is performed in which of the following state?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Chhattisgarh.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The "Gaur Maria" dance is a famous tribal folk dance performed by the Maria/Gond tribe of Chhattisgarh (Bastar region). Dancers wear headgear made of bison (gaur) horns. (गौर मारिया नृत्य — छत्तीसगढ़)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The dance imitates the movements of the bison and is performed with drums and flutes during festivals and weddings.

• Other folk dances of Chhattisgarh: Panthi, Raut Nacha, Karma, Sua and Pandwani (a folk narrative form).

NOTE

• Chhattisgarh was carved out of Madhya Pradesh in 2000; its capital is Raipur. It is rich in tribal culture and mineral resources.

question:
Match list I of cell organelles with their functions in list II.
List I: (a) Endoplasmic reticulum (b) Vacuoles (c) Golgi apparatus (d) Mitochondria
List II: (i) for packaging of materials synthesised near the ER and dispatching them to various targets. (ii) generates ATP. (iii) are storage sacs for solid or liquid contents. (iv) serve as channels for the transport of proteins.
solution_text:
The correct answer is (a) - (iv); (b) - (iii); (c) - (i); (d) - (ii).

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The correct matching of cell organelles with their functions is:

◦ (a) Endoplasmic reticulum → (iv) serve as channels for the transport of proteins.

◦ (b) Vacuoles → (iii) are storage sacs for solid or liquid contents.

◦ (c) Golgi apparatus → (i) packaging of materials synthesised near the ER and dispatching them.

◦ (d) Mitochondria → (ii) generates ATP.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Mitochondria is called the "powerhouse of the cell" because it produces ATP (energy currency).

• The Golgi apparatus is the "packaging and dispatch" centre; vacuoles store food, water and waste.

NOTE

• The Endoplasmic Reticulum is of two types: Rough ER (with ribosomes — protein synthesis) and Smooth ER (lipid synthesis).

question: Identify the INCORRECT pair.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Blossom Shower - Andhra Pradesh.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The INCORRECT pair is "Blossom Shower - Andhra Pradesh". Blossom Showers are actually associated with Karnataka (and Kerala), where they help coffee flowers to bloom — not Andhra Pradesh. (ब्लॉसम शावर — कर्नाटक, आंध्र प्रदेश नहीं)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Nor'Westers (Kalbaisakhi) — violent pre-monsoon thunderstorms of West Bengal/Assam.

• Bardoisila — pre-monsoon storms of Assam.

• Mango Shower — pre-monsoon rain of Kerala and coastal Karnataka that helps mangoes ripen.

NOTE

• Pre-monsoon showers benefit crops: Mango showers (mangoes), Blossom showers (coffee), while Kalbaisakhi helps jute and rice in Bengal/Assam.

question: In which state is the Jhumming cultivation known as Dahiya?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Madhya Pradesh.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Jhum (shifting) cultivation is known as "Dahiya" in Madhya Pradesh. It is a form of slash-and-burn agriculture practised by tribal communities. (झूम खेती को मध्य प्रदेश में 'दहिया' कहते हैं)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Shifting cultivation has different local names: Jhum (North-East India), Podu (Andhra Pradesh/Odisha), Bewar/Dahiya (Madhya Pradesh), Kumari (Western Ghats), Bringa (Odisha).

• In it, forest land is cleared and burned, cultivated for a few years, then abandoned.

NOTE

• Globally, shifting cultivation is called Milpa (Mexico), Ladang (Indonesia/Malaysia), Ray (Vietnam) and Roca (Brazil).

question: The first ICC Women's T20 Cricket World Cup was hosted by ________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is England.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The first ICC Women's T20 Cricket World Cup was hosted by England in 2009. It was won by England, who defeated New Zealand in the final. (पहला महिला टी20 विश्व कप — इंग्लैंड, 2009)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The first men's ICC T20 World Cup (2007) was hosted by South Africa and won by India (under M. S. Dhoni).

• Australia is the most successful team in the Women's T20 World Cup, having won it multiple times.

NOTE

• The ICC (International Cricket Council) headquarters is in Dubai, UAE. The Women's ODI World Cup began in 1973, even before the men's.

question: Who was named as the president of Shiv Sena (Shinde Group) during the party's national executive meeting in Mumbai in February 2023?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Eknath Shinde.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Eknath Shinde was named as the president of the Shiv Sena (Shinde Group) during the party's national executive meeting in Mumbai in February 2023. (एकनाथ शिंदे)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The Election Commission of India allotted the "Shiv Sena" name and the "bow and arrow" symbol to the Shinde faction in February 2023.

• Eknath Shinde became the Chief Minister of Maharashtra in June 2022 after a split in the undivided Shiv Sena.

NOTE

• The Shiv Sena was founded by Bal Thackeray in 1966. Uddhav Thackeray's faction was named Shiv Sena (Uddhav Balasaheb Thackeray).

question: Who among the following became the first Indian to win a gold medal at the World Athletics Championships event?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Neeraj Chopra.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Neeraj Chopra became the first Indian to win a gold medal at the World Athletics Championships by winning the javelin throw at the 2023 World Championships in Budapest, Hungary (with a throw of 88.17 m). (नीरज चोपड़ा)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Neeraj Chopra also won India's first-ever athletics Olympic gold in the Tokyo 2020 Olympics (held in 2021) in javelin throw.

• At the 2022 World Championships he had won silver, before taking gold in 2023.

NOTE

• The World Athletics Championships is organised by World Athletics (formerly IAAF). India's earlier medallist was Anju Bobby George (long jump bronze, 2003).

question: Which of the following Articles of the Constitution mentions that, “There shall be paid to the Judges of the Supreme Court, such salaries as may be determined by the Parliament by law, and until provision in that behalf is so made, such salaries as are specified in the Second Schedule”?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 125.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Article 125 of the Constitution deals with the salaries, etc., of the Judges of the Supreme Court. It provides that they shall be paid such salaries as Parliament determines by law, and until then, as specified in the Second Schedule. (अनुच्छेद 125 — उच्चतम न्यायालय के न्यायाधीशों का वेतन)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Article 124 — establishment and constitution of the Supreme Court.

• Article 126 — appointment of an acting Chief Justice.

• Article 127 — appointment of ad hoc judges.

NOTE

• Judges' salaries are charged on the Consolidated Fund of India and are non-votable, ensuring judicial independence.

question: Who is the writer of the novel ‘A Suitable Boy’?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Vikram Seth.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The novel "A Suitable Boy" (1993) was written by the Indian author Vikram Seth. It is one of the longest novels in the English language, set in post-Independence India. (विक्रम सेठ)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Vikram Seth's other famous works include "The Golden Gate" (a novel in verse) and "An Equal Music".

• "A Suitable Boy" was adapted into a BBC television series (2020).

NOTE

• Other authors: Aravind Adiga wrote "The White Tiger" (Booker Prize 2008); Neel Mukherjee wrote "The Lives of Others"

question: Which of the following initiatives of the Government of India promises 100 days of guaranteed wage employment to all the rural households who volunteer to do unskilled manual work?
option_1: Pradhan Mantri Garib Kalyan Rojgar Abhiyaan
option_2: Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Scheme
solution_text:
The correct answer is Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Scheme.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Scheme (MGNREGS/MGNREGA) guarantees 100 days of wage employment in a financial year to every rural household whose adult members volunteer to do unskilled manual work. (मनरेगा — 100 दिन का रोजगार)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• MGNREGA was enacted in 2005 and is implemented by the Ministry of Rural Development. It is the world's largest work guarantee programme.

• It provides a legal right to work and aims to enhance livelihood security in rural areas.

NOTE

• If work is not provided within 15 days, applicants are entitled to an unemployment allowance. At least one-third of beneficiaries must be women.

question: Who among the following personalities said, “What I object to is the ‘craze’ for machinery as such. The craze is for what they call labour-saving machinery. Men go on ‘saving labour’ till thousands are without work and thrown to the open streets to die of starvation.”?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Mahatma Gandhi.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The quotation objecting to the "craze for machinery" and labour-saving machinery that throws thousands out of work was said by Mahatma Gandhi. It reflects his philosophy favouring small-scale, village and cottage industries and human labour. (महात्मा गांधी)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Gandhi's economic ideas emphasised Swadeshi, self-sufficiency of villages (Gram Swaraj), the charkha (spinning wheel) and decentralised production.

• His views are elaborated in his work "Hind Swaraj" (1909).

NOTE

• Gandhi did not oppose machinery outright but opposed the exploitation and unemployment caused by blind mechanisation that ignored human welfare.
